iut_type: Review Page interpretation -- previewing public visibility before Submission, the precise meaning of a TCW ID shown instead of Yes/No, and blank auto-populated Member Detail fields
customer_question: Is there a way to confirm how our registration will appear to third parties once public, since some Review Page items may or may not actually be publicly displayed? Also, what does it mean that a field shows a TCW ID number (e.g., ES-25636) instead of a simple Yes/No? And are blank fields like Company City a problem?
question_variants: Is there a public preview mode for a registration before Submission?
Does a TCW reference always indicate a problem the registrant caused?
actual_issue: The customer, working with SIG's redesigned registration system for the first time, had three distinct points of confusion while reviewing their Review Page before finalizing: whether the page accurately represented what would become publicly visible, what a TCW reference number actually meant, and whether blank Member Detail fields would block registration.
plain_english_explanation: There is no formal public-preview feature before Submission -- after Submission, the Listing Owner can view the registration page even before the public disclosure date, but before Submission only the Review Page (an internal confirmation view, not necessarily an exact mirror of what becomes public) is viewable. The practical way to infer what will actually be publicly visible is to look at OTHER companies' already-published registrations with a similar structure (e.g., a single-DN-referenced registration matching your own registration's shape) and cross-reference their publicly displayed fields against the Review Page's field names. Regarding TCW: it stands for Test Case Waiver, and per SIG's 'Inter-Layer Dependencies' Help & Support page, it specifically applies when an Inter-Layer Dependency conflict that is SIG's OWN responsibility (i.e., baked into the referenced existing QDID combination, not something the registrant introduced) cannot otherwise be resolved -- entering the corresponding TCW ID number allows Submission to proceed (after SIG's confirmation/approval) despite the otherwise-unresolved dependency conflict. This is different from a registrant-caused inconsistency that the registrant could fix by editing their own ICS. Finally, regarding blank Member Detail fields (like Company City): these fields are auto-populated from the company's Member registration database and are not editable during the product registration process itself -- based on past experience, having them blank does not block a new product registration from completing. To actually fix them, the company's designated Primary Contact individual needs to separately request a correction to the company address in the Member registration database, outside of the product registration flow.
consultant_answer: There's no formal public preview before Submission -- after Submission, you (as Listing Owner) can view the page even before the public disclosure date, but beforehand only the Review Page is visible. To get a sense of what will actually be public, look at other companies' already-published registrations with a similar structure and compare their displayed fields against your Review Page's field names. TCW stands for Test Case Waiver -- see the 'Inter-Layer Dependencies' Help & Support page; in short, it applies when an Inter-Layer Dependency conflict that's SIG's own responsibility (built into the referenced QDID combination) can't otherwise be resolved, and entering the TCW ID lets Submission proceed after SIG's approval. And blank Member Detail fields like Company City are auto-populated from the Member database, not editable here, and don't block registration -- to fix them, have your Primary Contact request a correction to the Member registration database separately.
decision_logic: When a customer asks how to verify what will become publicly visible before Submission, point them to comparing already-published similar-structure registrations against the Review Page rather than claiming a formal preview exists; when a TCW ID appears instead of Yes/No, explain it specifically denotes a SIG-side inter-layer dependency conflict resolved via waiver, not a registrant-caused error; and reassure customers that blank, auto-populated Member Detail fields don't block registration, directing any correction request to the Primary Contact's separate Member-database update process.
final_recommendation: When a customer working with the redesigned registration system raises Review Page confusion, proactively explain the absence of a formal public preview (with the comparable-registration workaround), clarify TCW's specific SIG-side-fault scope, and distinguish Member Detail auto-populated fields (harmless if blank, fixed via a separate process) from the registrant's own ICS/Product List content.
risk_if_done_wrong: A customer might delay Submission unnecessarily worrying about blank Member Detail fields, or might misunderstand a TCW reference as indicating a registrant-caused defect requiring their own remediation when it actually reflects a SIG-side inter-layer dependency already accounted for via the waiver process.
